environmentalPersistence: Low — degraded by soil microbes within days; photolabile

lowDose.description: Promotes stem elongation, breaks seed dormancy, stimulates germination, promotes fruit set. Dramatically increases internode length and plant height. Used commercially to produce larger seedless grapes.

highDose.description: Excessive elongation produces weak, spindly stems prone to lodging. Leaf chlorosis from diluted chlorophyll in rapidly expanded cells. Reduced root development from shoot-biased growth. Reduced defense gene expression.

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Strongly negative (promotes height) at low dose; weak suppression at high dose via structural weakness
morphologicalEffects.leafSize: Increased at low dose; diluted/chlorotic at high dose
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Mild at high dose — weak tissue
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Mild at high dose — spindly stems cannot support water transport efficiently
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Absent at low dose; dilution chlorosis at high dose — rapidly expanded cells have less chlorophyll per unit area
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Mild at high dose — structural failure of weak tissue
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Mild reduction — GA suppresses anthocyanin biosynthesis (antagonizes JA/SA pigmentation)
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Mildly reduced — GA biases growth toward shoots at expense of roots
morphologicalEffects.stemThickness: Reduced — longer but thinner internodes at high dose
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: High dose effects most visible on newly formed, over-elongated tissue

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Absent at low dose; moderate at high dose (dilution effect, not degradation)
physiologyEffects.photosyntheticRate: Enhanced per plant at low dose (more leaf area); reduced per unit area at high dose
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Mildly increased at low dose; near-normal at high dose
physiologyEffects.waterUptake: Enhanced at low dose; mildly impaired at high dose

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Minimal — only at extreme high doses

microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Near-normal — GA does not strongly alter rhizosphere chemistry

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: 1–3 weeks — GA degrades rapidly; elongated internodes don't shrink but new growth normalizes
temporalDynamics.sensitization: None — DELLA re-accumulation restores sensitivity after exposure ends

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Low dose: taller, slightly lighter green. High dose: pale green/chlorotic, tall spindly stems
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Internodes — elongation is the primary visual signal
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Uniformly elongated — plants look like etiolated seedlings; less pigmented
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Low glow — GA3 conjugate signature; lower than all stress chemicals
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Moderate — elongated internodes persist; new growth normalizes; color recovers

synergies.synergyNote: GA + auxin is the classical elongation synergy — together they produce maximum cell elongation via complementary mechanisms (GA degrades DELLA; auxin activates expansins)
synergies.antagonismNote: GA antagonizes JA-mediated growth suppression — the DELLA-JAZ crosstalk. GA also opposes ABA-mediated dormancy and stress responses.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Endogenous plant hormone — present in all vascular plants; commercial GA3 from Fusarium fungal fermentation; used on grapes, cherries, citrus
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Commercially applied to seedless grapes (makes them larger), malting barley (uniform germination), citrus (delays rind aging), dwarf cereal crop development
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Very low — no significant human health risk
educationalContext.climateLink: GA signaling integrates temperature signals — flowering time and germination responses to climate are partly GA-mediated
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Both — commercial horticultural use; available for home gardening
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Why seedless grapes are so large — GA₃ is sprayed on them commercially. The story of how plant hormones are used as agricultural tools (and what happens when you over-apply).
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Food production technology, dwarf crop varieties (Green Revolution), plant-temperature interactions
